title: extra•ordinary — A Book on Everyday Creativity

summary.en: Co-authored, photographed and designed a book of new uses for ordinary objects with architect Hisako “Chako” Ichiki. After creating the book, built usable repurposed pieces for its Los Angeles gallery launch. Sold 11,000+ copies worldwide and was later featured in Japan’s DESIGN QUARTERLY.
summary.jp: 建築家のチャコと、日用品の新しい使い方を集めた本を共著。撮影と全ページのデザインを担当した。本の制作後、LAのギャラリーでの出版記念展に向け、実際に使える作品を制作。世界で1万1千部超が売れ、後にDESIGN QUARTERLYに掲載された。

creative.en: Three months of open-ended experiments became a book of reimagined everyday objects. Its first handmade prototype used a brush as its spine; the published book was followed by a gallery launch with usable repurposed furniture and installations.
creative.jp: 3か月の実験から、日用品の使い方を見立て直す本が生まれた。初期の手作り試作はブラシが背表紙。本の制作後には、実用的な家具やインスタレーションをつくり、ギャラリーで出版記念展を行った。

mine: Co-authored and art-directed the entire book
Photographed every concept, setting up controlled lighting and precise compositions
Designed every layout in Adobe InDesign, building a reading rhythm that mirrors the book's message of 'look closer, look differently'
Developed the Los Angeles book-launch exhibition after creating the book, building real usable pieces from repurposed everyday materials
Built exhibition furniture from unconventional materials
Pitched the book to more than ten publishers until Rockport Publishing said yes
team: Hisako Ichiki — architect, Bunch Design (Los Angeles) — co-developed the concept and experiments as co-author; individual contributions versus Takao's are not separated beyond 'co-author'

narrative.situation: This book began with no plan at all — a vague ambition to make something that would spark creativity in the people around them, with no idea what form it should take.

_notes: Co-authored with Hisako Ichiki; the page does not separate individual authorship contributions beyond crediting both as co-authors.
Engagement not explicitly stated; recorded as unstated rather than assumed own-venture, per the task's strict engagement rule.
2026-09-26: the brush spine belongs to the first handmade prototype (legacy page caption), not the published edition; the Solution was corrected to say so.

2026-10-10: Takao clarified the chronology: created the book first, then built real repurposed objects and usable furniture for its gallery book-launch event. Body expanded with retained original assets.

cardLine.en: A book of new uses for ordinary objects. Over 11,000 copies sold.
cardLine.jp: 日常の物の、別の使い方を集めた本。1 万 1 千部超。

oneLiner.en: A book of new uses for ordinary objects, followed by a hands-on gallery launch.
oneLiner.jp: 日用品の新しい使い方を集めた本と、実物を体験できる出版記念展。

challenge.en: The book began with no plan — three months of open experimentation in Los Angeles with architect Hisako “Chako” Ichiki, reimagining everyday objects. The hard part was turning unstructured play into a printed object that asks readers to look closer, and getting a publisher to say yes to something no category fit.
challenge.jp: この本は計画なしに始まった。建築家のチャコ（Hisako Ichiki）とロサンゼルスで 3 か月、日用品の使い道を考え直す実験を続けた。難しかったのは、形のない遊びを「もっと近くで、違う目で見て」と誘う印刷物にすること。そして、どの棚にも収まらない本に、出版社の「はい」をもらうことだった。

solution.en: We co-authored the book; I photographed the concepts and designed every page in InDesign. After creating it, we built real, usable repurposed pieces for its Los Angeles gallery launch, including furniture visitors could sit on. Rockport published the book after more than ten pitches. It sold 11,000+ copies worldwide and was later featured in Japan’s DESIGN QUARTERLY.
solution.jp: 本を共著し、私はアイデアの撮影とInDesignでの全ページのデザインを担当した。本の制作後、LAのギャラリーでの出版記念展に向け、来場者が座れる家具など、日用品を使った実用的な作品をつくった。10社以上に持ち込み、Rockportが刊行。世界で1万1千部超が売れ、その後DESIGN QUARTERLYに掲載された。

role.jp: 共著・アートディレクション・デザイン
